children: Wheat fell below $7 per bushel in late September, remaining near its lowest level since August 25 as traders assessed fresh details of the US-China trade agreement, including tariff reductions on agricultural products.
Both countries announced plans to lower tariffs on roughly $30 billion worth of imports from each side, covering a broad range of American farm goods including wheat.
The two sides also agreed to establish an agricultural working group to facilitate future negotiations and improve market access.

Still, traders are awaiting tangible signs of broader Chinese purchases, as progress has been limited on a separate pledge made during the Trump-Xi summit in May to buy an additional $17 billion worth of US agricultural products.

Elsewhere, traders continued to monitor Black Sea export flows after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy stated that India, Turkey, Egypt and other Middle Eastern countries were involved in efforts to restore safe shipping through the Black Sea.

title: Wheat Hits 1-Month Low
